trust_decision.summary: Once Connection.Tune negotiates frame_max, every inbound frame whose total size exceeds it must be rejected by the frame reader, on both transports; before the fix the reader was bounded only by the user-configured maxInboundMessageBodySize (64 MiB default), so the reader accepted frames up to that size regardless of the negotiated value.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the frame reader; Frame.readFrom is the only place an inbound payload length is validated, and an engineer reading the summary lands there and sees the limit coming from a configured field rather than from the negotiated frame_max.

fix_sites.module_kind: core connection / handshake (caller of the new setter)
transport SPI interface (new default no-op method)
second transport implementation (Netty) - looks out of scope

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Netty transport is opt-in (ConnectionFactory.java:1827) and its AmqpHandler already duplicates the size check, so a socket-only fix looks complete; the pre-negotiation window and the Netty decoder's buffer limit are then argued away as 'not the negotiated value' and 'just an allocation detail'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A frame whose total size is exactly frame_max must still be accepted (payload = frame_max - AMQCommand.EMPTY_FRAME_SIZE), hence the fix's '+1'; frame_max = 0 means 'no limit' and must not become a zero/negative cap (guarded by 'if (frameMax > 0)'); and a user-configured maxInboundMessageBodySize smaller than frame_max must keep applying via Math.min (ConnectionFactory.java:1679). Content header frames of exactly frame_max are already accepted outbound (AMQCommand.java:136-143).

O6_input_shapes: frame payload of exactly frame_max - AMQCommand.EMPTY_FRAME_SIZE bytes (total frame size = frame_max): must be accepted
frame payload of frame_max - EMPTY_FRAME_SIZE + 1 bytes (total = frame_max + 1): must be rejected
negotiated frame_max = 0 (unlimited in AMQP): no cap applied
ConnectionFactory#setMaxInboundMessageBodySize smaller than the negotiated frame_max: still wins (Math.min)
two transports: java.net.Socket reader (Frame.readFrom) and Netty inbound handler (AmqpHandler.channelRead)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Netty's LengthFieldBasedFrameDecoder is still constructed with maxFrameLength derived from maxInboundMessageBodySize (64 MiB default), so an oversized frame is fully buffered and allocated before AmqpHandler rejects it; the negotiated frame_max never reaches the decoder.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The handler rejects the frame at the API level anyway; the decoder's maxFrameLength is an allocation/layering concern, not the validation the report describes.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the Netty size check, 4 files from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Frames read before Connection.Tune are bounded only by maxInboundMessageBodySize: the main loop is already running (AMQConnection.java:334 initializes the handler, which starts the thread) while the negotiated cap is applied only after the tune value is computed at AMQConnection.java:428-431, so a Connection.Start or Connection.Tune frame of up to 64 MiB is accepted.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: No frame_max has been negotiated yet during the handshake, so the advisory's bound cannot apply to Connection.Start/Tune frames.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the fix's call site

O8_uncovered_routes.route: AMQConnection's public constructor accepts any FrameHandler (AMQConnection.java:218-220) and ConnectionFactory#createConnection is protected (ConnectionFactory.java:1406-1409); a handler that does not override the new method keeps the interface's no-op default, so its inbound frames remain bounded only by whatever it was constructed with.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The fix deliberately makes the SPI method a default no-op for source/binary compatibility; third-party frame handlers are the user's code and out of the library's scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, interface file separate from both transports

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a separate setter for a maximum inbound frame payload size, distinct from the message-body limit
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The client already exposes the reader limit as a configuration knob and threads it through both frame handler factories (ConnectionFactory.java:1080, 1093), so a maintainer adding a second knob is natural.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third public SocketFrameHandler constructor taking both an inbound message-body limit and an inbound frame limit
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class already has two constructors whose only difference is the size argument (SocketFrameHandler.java:68-70 and 75-83).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a Frame.readFrom overload without a limit, or one that derives the limit from the frame type
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Frame is a public wire-format utility used by tools and tests, and readFrom is already public static with a caller-supplied bound.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a recovery path that recreates the frame handler without re-applying the negotiated frame_max
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Recovery rebuilds connections through the same AMQConnection#start handshake, so state that must be re-applied per connection is a natural place for a sibling omission.

O9_family: Improper input validation (CWE-20) of inbound AMQP frame length against the negotiated frame_max, with memory-exhaustion impact

O10_build.toolchain: Maven (pom.xml; source/target 1.8, maven-compiler-plugin 3.15.0, surefire; JUnit 5.14.4, AssertJ 3.27.7, Netty 4.2.15.Final)
services: RabbitMQ broker only for the project's functional/integration tests; the affected frame-reader path needs none
O10_build.project_tests: FrameMax.java (functional, needs a broker: negotiation, frame sizes, oversize rejection), BrokenFramesTest (drives AMQConnection with a mock FrameHandler), UnexpectedFrames (functional); the fix adds NegotiatedFrameMaxInboundTest, a loopback-only unit test that is absent at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Set the reader's limit to frameMax in SocketFrameHandler (or Frame.readFrom) once, forgetting the EMPTY_FRAME_SIZE +1 boundary, the frame_max = 0 no-limit case, and the Netty AmqpHandler copy of the same check.
